statement: Every order-three action in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group has exactly two full profinite section conjugacy classes, each with zero first mod-three cohomology of its fixed subgroup. Its cusp normalizer is torsion-free, and the cube of a lift of the labeled outer generator has a 3-adic cusp exponent which is a unit.
where_proved: Part D, statement D.48; work/part_c/d48.tex; code/part_c/torus_order3_sections_d48.py
depends_on: A.2; A.7; D.27; D.32; D.33; full-profinite Brown restriction; the explicit coefficient Bockstein and cyclic-resolution periodicity
manuscript_passages: Part D(b) of the task; §24, folio 147 verso, scan 293; §30, folios 194–196, scans 383–387; §31, folios 198–199 verso, scans 391–394.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The full semidirect abelianization, coefficient Bockstein, spectral-sequence period map, section normalizers, finite-cover boundary characters and peripheral norm equation are explicit.
notes: D.33 forces the nontrivial 3-adic two-dimensional cyclotomic action. Its coinvariant group has order three, so the full extension has maximal pro-three abelian quotient C3 squared. No nonzero mod-three character lifts to Z/9; the two Bocksteins force collapse and periodic injectivity in the rank-two spectral sequence. A unique section would make the Bockstein of the character vanishing on that section restrict to zero on its normalizer, contradicting full Brown restriction. Exactly two section classes and zero first fixed-subgroup cohomology follow. A finite-cover boundary character prevents those fixed subgroups from containing the full cusp Z3; hence the cusp normalizer is torsion-free and its cube exponent is a 3-adic unit. The global multiplier and full conjugacy problems remain open.
